hints: Think about the order the phases happen in: which of anaphase, metaphase, prophase and telophase comes first in mitosis?
Recall when the spindle normally starts to form from microtubules, and ask yourself which phase would notice it missing first.
walkthrough:
**Recall the order of mitosis**

Think of mitosis as a story in order. It runs prophase, then metaphase, then anaphase, then telophase.

So the earliest phase listed here is prophase.

**Remember what the spindle does and when it forms**

The spindle is made of microtubules. It starts to form during prophase as the centrioles move apart.

It is then used in metaphase to line up chromosomes and in anaphase to pull chromatids apart.

**Pick the first phase to be hit**

If a drug stops the spindle forming, the cell will notice this as soon as it tries to make the spindle.

That is in prophase, before it can even get to metaphase or anaphase. So the answer is C.

options.A: Anaphase needs the spindle to pull chromatids apart, but it happens after prophase and metaphase, so it is not the first to be affected.
options.B: Metaphase needs the spindle to line chromosomes on the equator, but the spindle should already have formed in prophase, so this is too late.
options.C: Correct. The spindle begins to form in prophase, so preventing its formation affects prophase first.
options.D: Telophase is the last stage of mitosis, when nuclei reform, so it cannot be the first phase affected.
